findings.highlight: She even spread the rumor to other schools
findings.evidenceJa: あいつらなんか大喜びでさ…交流試合やってた他校の連中にまでメール流してんの。
findings.explanation: The subject is Matsui and the other former club members: they are delighted by Koharu's disgrace and are circulating the email even to players at other schools. The English switches from that hostile group to a singular 'she,' obscuring the coordinated retaliation that explains why the rumor has spread so far.
findings.japanese:
「あいつらなんか大喜びでさ…
交流試合やってた他校の連中にまでメール流してんの。
副キャプテン、あっちの男子にも人気あったし」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, her whole group seems overjoyed… She even spread the rumor to other schools who participated in the interleague match. The vice-captain was popular with the boys there too, after all."

findings.evidenceJa: 必ず日付が変わる時間に掛かってくる。
findings.explanation: Koharu always calls at the time the date changes—that is, at midnight. The English relocates every call to before midnight, contradicting the immediately stated 00:15 time during a thirty-minute call and breaking the precisely described ritual around which Haruki now structures his studying.
findings.japanese:
要するに、毎日３０分。
必ず日付が変わる時間に掛かってくる。
findings.todokanai: More precisely, for 30 minutes every day. And always right before midnight.

findings.highlight: before she decided to take matters into her own hands
findings.evidenceJa: 小春は、俺がこうして太鼓判を押す前から、俺を救うためにあいつらを頼ってた。
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes that Koharu had already relied on Takeya and Io to save him before he now gave them his personal seal of approval. The English invents a later decision by Koharu to 'take matters into her own hands,' replacing the actual temporal contrast and weakening Haruki's recognition that her judgment of his friends preceded his endorsement.
findings.japanese:
小春は、俺がこうして太鼓判を押す前から、
俺を救うためにあいつらを頼ってた。
findings.todokanai: Koharu had sought out those two for help in order to save me before she decided to take matters into her own hands.

findings.evidenceJa: 一字一句、互いに噛みしめながら紡いでいく不器用な会話。
findings.explanation: The two awkwardly weave the conversation while each carefully weighs and absorbs every single word. 'Spoken through clenched teeth' conventionally signals anger or hostility, imposing the opposite emotional register on an exchange defined by tenderness, hesitation, and mutual self-denial.
findings.japanese:
昔の長電話みたいに自然と言葉が湧いてくることのない、
一字一句、互いに噛みしめながら紡いでいく不器用な会話。
findings.todokanai: Unlike my long telephone conversations three years ago where words came out naturally, now every word and phrase is awkward, and spoken through clenched teeth.
